newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open higher before PPI, FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open higher before PPI, FOMC meeting.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened slightly higher on Wednesday ahead of the U.S. October report on wholesale prices and a Federal Reserve policy meeting, two events investors believe will be benign for the bond market.
The 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond was up 2/32 to 100-26/32, yielding 6.44 percent.

The market gets the October Producer Price Index (PPI) report at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, that wholesale prices rose a mild 0.2 percent during the month, after a 0.2 percent September rise.
Without food and energy items, the PPI is expected to be up a slight 0.1 percent, after a 0.3 percent September gain.

The forecast of economists Sally Kleinman and Madeline Strobing at Chase Securities differed somewhat from the consensus as garnered from the Reuters poll. The Chase economists expect the total PPI to be up 0.3 percent and the core PPI to be down 0.1 percent.
The Chase economists said their below-trend PPI is based on weak passenger car and light truck prices, which tend to be volatile at this time of year when new models are introduced.
The meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, the policy-making arm of the Federal Reserve, scheduled for today is expected to be a market non-event.

With unanimity, economists expect the central bank to leave interest rates unchanged at this meeting, the Fed having gotten, at least for now, its desired mix of slower economic growth and fairly restrained inflation.

Matthew Alexy, chief markets strategist at CS First Boston, said the PPI data would be interesting for the market but that data due on Thursday on October consumer prices and retail sales would probably be a little more influential.

Alexy said there's some "general hope that the market backs up a little bit because there are some people who want to get involved." But he said it could turn out that those players will be forced into the market by a market move up.

"People are at the point here where a move up will force a response," said Alexy. "The market will be rallying and they'll have (portfolio) duration considerations. I don't think there are a lot of big profit-takers."
Alexy said the market's ability to hold Tuesday's gains overnight "says a lot as well.
"The market is comfortable at these levels," he said.
In early trade, three- and six-month bill rates were unchanged at 5.03 percent and 5.07 percent, respectively. Year bill rates were down one basis points to 5.14 percent.
Two-year notes were unchanged at 100-9/32 to yield 5.72 pct. Five-year notes were unchanged at 101-5/32 to yield 5.98 percent.
Ten-year notes were unchanged at 102-9/32, yielding 6.19 percent.
